title: release annotations and profile-migration pipeline for staged model variant groups
author: Priya Mukherjee
description: Motivation: onboarding model variant groups (multi-variant releases and staged rollouts) requires richer release metadata and a safe migration path for existing profile records. This PR introduces: 1) release annotations attached to model profiles (human-readable and machine tags) to drive changelog generation and automated rollout guards; 2) a profile-migration pipeline that can reconcile legacy single-profile manifests into variant groups with compatibility metadata; 3) a templated release-notes renderer that consumes annotations and evaluation summaries to produce concise draft changelogs suitable for publishing. Design goals: keep runtime serving behavior unchanged, enable automated generation of release notes, and provide a reversible migration plan with a dry-run mode. Summary of changes: - schema: add `release_annotations` and `variant_group_id` fields to profile manifest schema with validation and backfill hooks - migration: new CLI subcommand `registry migrate-variants` with --dry-run and --apply modes; supports mapping rules and conflict resolution strategy - templating: Jinja-based release-note templates plus a small renderer to pull top-k regressions/wins from recent evals - tests: unit tests for schema validation, migration logic, and note rendering; E2E smoke test that runs a dry-run migration on a snapshot - observability: emitted events for migration steps and a new metric `registry.migrations.applied` Migration plan: 1. run `registry migrate-variants --dry-run --snapshot <path>` to see proposed groupings and warnings 2. review proposed release_annotations (UI and CSV export added) 3. run with --apply in a maintenance window; migration is idempotent and records a migration_id 4. optionally trigger `registry render-release-notes --migration-id <id> --template default` Rollout: default to dry-run for 2 weeks, then allow opt-in applies for new onboardings. Backwards compatibility: existing code paths that read model profiles ignore unknown annotation fields; schema validators are permissive when `compat_mode` is enabled. Testing: added unit tests and a small integration scenario in testdata/variant-snapshots. Security: annotations are treated as metadata only; no execution. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-5512 (profile provenance) and pairs with the release assembler components. Checklist: - [x] schema and validators - [x] CLI and dry-run - [x] rendering templates - [x] tests and E2E smoke - [x] docs snippet in registry/README.md - [x] metrics/events emitted

review_thread: Ethan Ross: Design looks sound. Two high-level asks: (1) show an example of a migration conflict and how operator should resolve, (2) ensure expensive backfills are rate-limited and observable.

Priya Mukherjee: Added a conflict-resolution policy and CSV export to let operators resolve conflicts offline. Backfill uses a token-bucket limiter and emits `registry.migrations.backfill_rate` metrics; documented in the README.
Lina Park: The release_notes renderer should redact private eval identifiers by default. Also prefer a deterministic sort for regression lists so notes are stable across runs.
Priya Mukherjee: Renderer now redacts eval ids and sorts regressions by delta descending then name; added unit tests to assert determinism.
Marco Hernández: Minor nit: please add telemetry to indicate number of profiles upgraded per migration_id. Also flag for reindexing downstream caches after apply.

Priya Mukherjee: Emitting `registry.migrations.profiles_upgraded` and `registry.migrations.reindex_required` event when reindex is needed; reindex step left as an explicit operator action to avoid surprise traffic spikes.
ci_summary: CI passed on GitHub Actions: unit matrix (py38/py39), lint (ruff), mypy; flaky integration retry on second run cleared the transient failure.
release_notes: Add variant-group-aware profile metadata and a migration CLI to convert legacy single-profile manifests into variant groups. Introduces release_annotations to improve changelog generation and a templated renderer for concise release notes. Includes dry-run mode, CSV export for operator review, and metrics for migration observability.
notes_for_changelog: Users can run `registry migrate-variants --dry-run` to preview changes. This is non-breaking and reversible; a production apply requires operator review. See docs/registry/variant_migration.md for examples.
qa_instructions: Run `pytest registry/tests` and `python -m registry.cli migrate-variants --dry-run --snapshot testdata/variant-snapshots/sample-legacy-manifest.json`. Verify CSV export and rendered draft in changelog/draft/2024-11-variant-migration.md.
